name: Dokploy
description: Your own Vercel, Heroku or Netlify. Deploy apps and databases on MOS with a few clicks

paths.name: Data
paths.description: Dokploy's database (postgres/), plus .better_auth_secret and .postgres_password, this install's own keys made on first start. Back this folder up.

paths.name: .Docker
paths.description: Docker registry logins Dokploy uses to pull and push your images.

paths.name: AppData
paths.description: Dokploy's working folder on MOS: Traefik settings and certificates, app source code, compose files, logs and backups. It must be /etc/dokploy on the host too, because Dokploy hands these paths to Docker.

paths.name: Docker.Sock
paths.description: The Docker socket. Dokploy uses it to set up Docker Swarm, Postgres and Traefik and to build and run your apps. This gives Dokploy full control of Docker on MOS.

ports.name: Web UI
ports.description: Dokploy dashboard, published on host as 6183

variables.name: TZ
variables.description: Your time zone, like Europe/London or America/New_York.

variables.name: TRAEFIK_PORT
variables.description: The port your deployed apps are served on over http. Not 80, which MOS uses itself. To reach apps by domain from the internet, forward port 80 on your router to this port. Change it before the first start; afterwards change it in Dokploy under Web Server > Traefik too.

variables.name: TRAEFIK_SSL_PORT
variables.description: The port your deployed apps are served on over https. Not 443. To reach apps by domain from the internet, forward port 443 on your router to this port. Change it before the first start, like TRAEFIK_PORT.
